note: Literature notes that developmental delay/intellectual disability differentiates Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome from related LDS presentations, though SMAD2-related LDS clinical descriptions include varying reports of craniofacial and neurocognitive features.

evidence.text: Developmental delay and intellectual disability serve as differentiating features of Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome relative to LDS subtypes including SMAD2/3-related conditions.

evidence.text: The phenotypic spectrum of SMAD2-related Loeys-Dietz syndrome has been discussed in relation to features including intellectual disability/learning difficulties and craniosynostosis.
